messages:
Priya Sharma: Quick question — when we expose bulk-edit for SLO thresholds in the console, should quiet windows be handled as an attribute on the SLO or as a separate notify-policy resource?

Alex Chen: leaning toward separate notify-policy. makes reuse and rollout safer (no accidental threshold change + quiet window).

Jae Park: separate resource + attach by reference. we also need to support a bulk patch that can atomically swap references for a set of SLOs during a rollout.

Priya Sharma: problem is product wants 'edit thresholds across N services and optionally keep existing notify rules' (copy behavior). UI needs a simple toggle. API needs to be explicit.

Samir: agree. If we keep quiet-window on SLO, bulk-edit becomes risky — you might override per-tenant exceptions. If it's a notify-policy, a bulk-edit could create a new policy and point all SLOs to it.

Maya G.: also consider telemetry: we need to know whether a change was a threshold vs a notify-policy swap for regression alerts. Right now our audit log just shows "config changed".

Priya Sharma: telemetry note is big — Product wants rollbacks and regression detection by type. can we tag config changes with delta-type: threshold|notify-swap|quiet-window?

Alex Chen: definitely. backend can add an enum in change events. small api proto change: add field 'change_type' in /config/changes.

Jae Park: pseudo-payload (for API team):
```json
{
  "op": "bulk_patch",
  "slo_ids": ["slo-123","slo-456"],
  "threshold_patch": {"p95": 300},
  "notify_policy_ref": "np-2024-05",
  "dry_run": true,
  "change_type": "threshold_and_notify_swap"
}
```

Samir: +1 but add: "preserve_overrides": true|false so tenant-specific overrides won't be clobbered unless caller opts-in.

Priya Sharma: good call. UX: default preserve_overrides=true, show a preview diff with how many tenants have overrides.

Maya G.: about previews: console should show estimated alert volume delta after the bulk change (using current traffic + sampling). Please don't make us run full sim for every preview. a quick heuristic is fine.

Alex Chen: we can reuse the telemetry sampling pipeline: run a lightweight pass on last 7 days with sampling factor. output: estimated alerts/day and 95% CI. show per-tenant top-5 impacts.

Priya Sharma: rollout UX: can we stage the update by percent of tenants? 10% -> 30% -> 100% with automatic pause on alert spike.

Jae Park: routing-wise: when we change notify-policy we should honor existing escalation/fallback routes. that means new policy must declare compatible contact bindings or we fallback to previous policy for affected tenants during canary.

Samir: implement as: create new policy, apply to canary tenants (by tag). If any tenant sees > X spike, auto-roll back that tag.

Maya G.: add instrumentation: create a short-lived eval that tracks alert rate/latency/duplicates for canary tenants and surface in the rollout UI.

Priya Sharma: final question for API owners — what's the easiest backwards-compatible way to expose preserve_overrides and change_type? 1) add optional fields to bulk endpoint 2) create a separate /bulk-rollout endpoint

Alex Chen: option 1 is fine, but make it explicit in schema and server-side validation. prefer not to add new endpoint unless we need different auth/scopes.

Jae Park: okay to ship option 1. we'll version the proto (v2) and keep old behavior if fields absent.

alert-bot: Deploy started: cfg-service v2.14.1 -> staging

Priya Sharma: thanks — we'll draft product copy for the console (preview, preserve overrides, canary steps) and the API change doc. I'll create a short RFC and link it here. :thumbsup: 

Alex Chen: tag me on the RFC please. I'll handle the telemetry delta API.

Samir: I'll prototype the preview heuristic tomorrow.

Jae Park: will add server-side validation + rollback hooks.

Maya G.: adding request for change_type in audit schema to my backlog.

Priya Sharma: participant ok? looks like we covered UX+API+telemetry+rollout behavior. closing this thread once RFC is up.
